title: Submitting & Validating Forms ✅
description: Handle `action`, `method`, and use HTML5 validation attributes like `required` and `pattern`.

slides.title: How Forms Send Data 📨
slides.content:
# The `action` and `method` Attributes

- `action` – the URL where the form data is sent.
- `method` – the HTTP method: `GET` (appends data to URL) or `POST` (sends data in request body).

```html
<form action="/search" method="get">
  <input type="text" name="query">
  <button>Search</button>
</form>
```
Use `GET` for search queries (bookmarkable), `POST` for sensitive or large data (login, uploads).

slides.title: The Submit Button 🚀
slides.content:
# Triggering the Form

Several ways to submit:
- `<button type="submit">` – the most flexible; can contain text and HTML.
- `<input type="submit">` – simpler, self‑closing.
- `<input type="image">` – an image as a submit button.

Pressing `Enter` inside a text field will also submit the form (if there's only one input or a submit button exists).

quizData.question: Which HTTP method is suitable for a login form to keep credentials private?
quizData.explanation: `POST` sends data in the request body, not visible in the URL, unlike `GET`.

slides.title: HTML5 Validation Attributes ✅
slides.content:
# Catch Errors Before They Reach the Server

You can enforce rules directly in HTML, no JavaScript needed:
- `required` – the field must be filled.
- `minlength` / `maxlength` – length of text.
- `min` / `max` – numeric range.
- `pattern` – a regular expression the value must match.

```html
<input type="text" name="zip" pattern="[0-9]{5}" title="Five‑digit ZIP code" required>
```
The `title` attribute provides the error hint.

slides.title: A Validated Form
slides.content: A sign‑up form with client‑side validation:
slides.codeSnippet:
<form action="/signup" method="post">
  <label for="email">Email:</label>
  <input type="email" id="email" name="email" required>

  <label for="password">Password:</label>
  <input type="password" id="password" name="password" minlength="8" required>

  <label for="age">Age:</label>
  <input type="number" id="age" name="age" min="13" max="120">

  <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>

slides.title: Disabling and Read‑only Fields 🛑
slides.content:
# Prevent User Changes

- `disabled` – the control is greyed out, and its value is **not** submitted.
- `readonly` – the value is visible and submitted, but cannot be edited.

```html
<input type="text" value="Progly" readonly>
```
Use them for fields that display fixed data.

quizData.question: If a field has `disabled`, its value will still be sent when the form is submitted.
quizData.explanation: Disabled fields are not submitted. Use `readonly` if you want the value submitted but not editable.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Always Validate on the Server Too

Client‑side validation is for user convenience; it can be bypassed. Always perform server‑side validation for security.
